items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: he showed me this placard that he's got with my name all over it and Johnny Griffin and Jody Christian and Phil Thomas on drums

ctx.x: No. The latter part of '59, around November, some guy come out of Chicago -- he's dead now --

you know, a fellow named Don[Defore]-- he come up with the big idea that he'd come to New York -- and he had signed Johnny Griffin and Johnny was back in Chicago then, and he wanted Sonny Rollins, and he's gonna get John Coltrane; each one of wanted them to come and play a concert at the University of Chicago. He was promoting it like that.

So he comes and finds me and says, well, you know how people are -- this particular night, I just happened to hanging out in front of the Birdland, and Tommy Potter was working downstairs with somebody, and like, musicians -- we didn't have dressing rooms. I mean in all those big clubs, you didn't have no place where the musicians could go and sit after you got off the bandstand. You couldn't sit at the tables, as that was for customers.
